findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-26: the key 'B bad 2, then C 0' is correct (Node 24 prints 'B bad 2' then 'C 0'). But choosing it over distractors 'B bad 2 only' (line 210) and 'B bad 2, then C undefined' (line 211) turns on one fact: catch returns a new promise fulfilled with the handler's return value, so a then after a catch still runs and receives that value. No learner page states this for catch. html-css-js/dom-tooling-and-async/promises/artifact.html says 'then returns a new promise ... Whatever a callback returns becomes the next value' in the then paragraph, and every page example ends the chain at catch ('catch handles any rejection earlier in the chain'). A learner who reads catch as the end of the chain can defend 'B bad 2 only'.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to the promises page (Activity 3): 'catch also returns a new promise; if its callback returns normally, the chain is fulfilled again with that value, so a later then runs.' Otherwise replace the item with a chain that ends at catch.

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-23: the stem describes Help as 'an a element holding only an icon, with aria-label="Help"' and never mentions href. An a element without href is not a link and is not in the Tab order, which would itself be a keyboard barrier. html-css-js/html-and-css/accessibility-basics/artifact.html teaches '<a href> over role="link"' (navigation for free), so a careful learner may wonder whether Help is also a barrier. Distractors C and D (lines 179-180) then call it 'the icon link'.
findings.recommendation: Write 'Help: a link (<a href="/help">) holding only an icon, with aria-label="Help"; Tab reaches it.'

findings.claim: html-css-js-final-mcq-19: the key ('Number ... loses precision above Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER; keep such ids as BigInt') is right on cause, and the stem's values are accurate (Node 24: JSON.parse('{"id":9007199254740993}').id prints 9007199254740992). But the feedback does not say that the id has to avoid becoming a Number at all. Once res.json() has made it a Number the digit is gone, so converting the arrived Number to BigInt cannot restore it. In practice the service sends such ids as strings. A learner could read the key as 'wrap the arrived id in BigInt'. The pages teach only BigInt literals (javascript-fundamentals/javascript-for-java-developers), not converting a string.
findings.recommendation: Extend the key feedback: '... BigInt holds exact large integers, but the id must not pass through Number first, so have the service send it as a string and keep it as a string or BigInt.'
